verify_research.acceptance: seleccion unica/multiple segun contrato y readback
verify_research.contract_observed: Current state schema exposes one selectedId, so current implemented contract is single-selection, not multi-selection.
source_evidence: actions.js SELECT returns state with selectedId=action.id
REMOVE_COMPONENT clears selectedId when removing selected component
renderLayers applies active only when state.selectedId===layer id and layer click dispatches SELECT
renderCanvas applies selected only when state.selectedId===node id and node click dispatches SELECT
touch pointer begin sets selectedId to moved item and persists it
verify_research.dedup: No evidence of a multi-select requirement or second selection engine. A product patch to introduce selectedIds would violate minimum-delta policy without a demonstrated requirement.

execute_delta.reason: Single-selection state is internally consistent across reducer, layers, canvas, editor and touch selection; no reproduced product failure justifies source mutation.

test_report.static_microtest: PASS reducer/readback invariant: SELECT replaces the sole selectedId; therefore selecting B after A cannot retain A in selection state.
test_report.functional_readback: PASS layers, canvas and property editor all derive selection from the same selectedId.
test_report.runtime_evidence_gap: No dedicated fresh browser assertion for switching A->B was found; independent reviewer should add/execute it before VERIFIED_CLOSED.
simulations: S1 add A -> selectedId=A -> A layer/node active
S2 add/select B -> selectedId=B -> A no longer satisfies active predicate
S3 remove selected B -> selectedId=null -> editor returns no-selection state
refutations: R1 searched for selectedIds/multi-selection and found no parallel contract
R2 checked both layer and canvas selectors to reject a UI-only selection illusion
R3 checked REMOVE_COMPONENT and touch pointer path to reject stale selectedId on deletion/touch
